Find applicable evidence-backed ways to reduce execution time in this GitHub Actions workflow. Consider its jobs, dependencies, commands, triggers, and repository manifests.
name: Kernel e2e tests

on:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  test:
    name: Linux ${{ matrix.kernel }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        kernel: ["5.10", "5.15", "6.1", "6.6", "6.12", "stable", "mainline"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-build-environment

      # Download dependencies for the host build.
      - name: Download Go dependencies
        run: go mod download

      - name: Install VM and trigger dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install --yes make qemu-system-x86 iproute2 iputils-ping curl python3
          CGO_ENABLED=0 go install lmb.io/vimto@latest
          echo "$(go env GOPATH)/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          sudo chmod 0666 /dev/kvm

      - name: Build test binaries on host
        run: make -j"$(nproc)" all

      # Fail early on image/boot problems instead of consuming the entire job.
      # SIGINT lets vimto stop QEMU and print its buffered boot console.
      - name: Check kernel VM boots
        env:
          KERNEL_IMAGE: ghcr.io/cilium/ci-kernels:${{ matrix.kernel }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          timeout --signal=INT --kill-after=30s 5m \
            vimto -kernel "$KERNEL_IMAGE" exec -- /bin/uname -a < /dev/null 2>&1 | tee kernel-boot.log

      - name: Run e2e tests in VM
        timeout-minutes: 31
        env:
          KERNEL_IMAGE: ghcr.io/cilium/ci-kernels:${{ matrix.kernel }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          timeout --signal=INT --kill-after=30s 30m \
            vimto -kernel "$KERNEL_IMAGE" exec -- /bin/bash scripts/test-kernel.sh < /dev/null 2>&1 | tee kernel-e2e.log

      - name: Upload guest logs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: kernel-e2e-${{ matrix.kernel }}
          path: |
            kernel-boot.log
            kernel-e2e.log
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 14

name: Checks

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # submodules: the SoloPlay submodule cannot be checked in isolation (its tsconfig points at
      # ../../sdk and ../../libs), so the parent checkout is where it gets validated - against the
      # exact commit this repo pins.
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      # Node 24: eslint-plugin-es-x@10 requires ^22.23.0 || ^24.18.0 || >=26.4.0, and
      # eslint@10 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24. Anything older cannot run the toolchain.
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # lint:check, never `lint` - that one is `eslint --fix`, which would rewrite files in CI
      # and let anything auto-fixable pass silently.
      - name: ESLint
        run: npm run lint:check

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      # The no-undef inventory is generated. If someone adds a global without regenerating,
      # the committed file goes stale and no-undef quietly stops covering it.
      - name: Globals inventory is current
        run: npm run globals:check

      - name: Typecheck (SoloPlay submodule)
        run: npm run typecheck:soloplay

      # Every runtime .js must belong to a TS program. A file in none gets no typechecking and
      # no editor intellisense, and nothing else reports it.
      - name: No orphaned files
        run: node tools/audit/program-files.mjs --check
